newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel plans year/year rise in aluminium sales.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel plans year/year rise in aluminium sales.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd, Japan's largest aluminium maker, said it plans to sell 29,850 tonnes of flat-rolled and extruded aluminium products per month in the half-year to March 1997.
This would be up 4.7 percent from the same period a year ago but down 8.7 percent from this year's April-September period.
The estimates include sales from a rolling mill in Australia which Kobe Steel owns jointly with Aluminum Co of America.
The company plans sales of flat-rolled products at 26,000 tonnes per month, up 3.2 percent year-on-year but off 10.5 percent from April-September.
Kobe Steel plans extruded product sales of 3,850 tonnes per month, up 16.3 percent year-on-year and up 5.2 percent from the previous half-year.
With regard to its brass output, the company said it planned sales of 10,800 tonnes per month, off 4.9 percent year-on-year and unchanged from the April-September period.

Kobe Steel said in a statement that while a modest improvement in the economy was expected to continue in the half-year ahead, it did not feel this would be sufficient to lift overall demand for the company's brass and aluminium products. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-6179
